body.statement: Apply the published rank-two deterministic count certificate to the canonical anchor hypergraph. For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) with generic factor rows, if \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\), then every coordinate of \(\mu(P)\) is a functional of the entire observed law \(P_O\), and that functional is the construction in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-functional}\). If \(r_{1,2}(H_3)<T-2\), then \(\ker\overline R(P)\supsetneq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\), and there is a two-dimensional subspace \(\widetilde{\mathcal L}\neq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\) such that \((\widetilde{\mathcal L})_{S_c}=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\) for every \(c\in[C]\). Thus certificate failure implies generic nonuniqueness of the factor plane. It does not, under the frozen primitive assumptions alone, imply causal-target nonidentification: those assumptions permit a nonempty certificate-failing specification on which \(\mu(P)=0\) for every \(P\in\mathcal M\).
body.justification: The theorem transports the published generic count certificate into an explicit complete-observed-law identifying functional when the certificate passes and proves factor-plane nonuniqueness as the exact unconditional algebraic consequence when it fails.
body.gap: Published count and pebble results do not derive the observed conditional eigenspaces or the causal mean map. Conversely, the frozen primitive model includes a nonempty tight-radius certificate-failing specification with a constant zero target, so complete-observed-law countermodels with different missing means cannot be asserted without further restrictions.
body.consumer: A passing certificate licenses complete untreated-mean recovery for Lei--Ross \(\operatorname{apm}\) and Liu--Wang--Xu \(\operatorname{fect}\); a failing certificate warns of factor-plane ambiguity but does not itself certify causal-target nonidentification.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\). All conditional moments used below exist by \(\texttt{ass:moment-radius}\), and conditioning on cohort \(c\) is legitimate because \(p_c\geq p_\star>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:positive-shares}\). Write \(\mathcal L=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\). By \(\texttt{ass:rank-two-factor-law}\) and \(\texttt{ass:error-mean}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\nu_c
&=\mathbb E_P[J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c]\\
&=\mathbb E_P[\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c]\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.                                             \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:loading-error-orthogonality}\) and \(\texttt{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
V_c
&=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c)\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}
  +\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c)\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.    \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
The first summand in (2) has rank two and second eigenvalue at least \(g_\star>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\). Hence the two leading eigenvalues of \(V_c\) strictly exceed \(\sigma_c^2\), while all remaining eigenvalues equal \(\sigma_c^2\). It follows that
\[
\Pi_2(V_c)=\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})},
\qquad
Q_c=I_{|S_c|}-\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})}.           \tag{3}
\]
The complete observed law \(P_O\) determines \(p_c\), the conditional mean \(\nu_c\), and the conditional covariance \(V_c\), because \(p_c>0\). Therefore it determines every local plane in (3).

Choose the matrices \(B_c\) as in \(\texttt{def:relation-operator}\). Since \(B_c^{\prime}B_c=Q_c\), for every \(y\in\mathbb R^{|S_c|}\),
\[
\|B_cy\|^2=y^{\prime}Q_cy,
\]
so \(\ker B_c=\ker Q_c=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\). The positive weights \(p_c\) then give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal K(P):=\ker\overline R(P)
&=\bigcap_{c=1}^C\ker(B_cJ_c)\\
&=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^T:x_{S_c}\in
       \operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\text{ for every }c\in[C]\right\}. \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal K(P)\). Although the individual orthonormal row bases \(B_c\) are not unique, (4) shows that \(\mathcal K(P)\) is uniquely determined by \(P_O\).

By \(\texttt{lem:generic-rank-two-coordinate-projection-certificate}\), on the generic locus imposed by \(\texttt{ass:generic-factor-rows}\), the local planes in (3) determine \(\mathcal L\) uniquely if and only if the anchor multihypergraph contains a set \(F\) of \(T-2\) triples satisfying
\[
|F'|\leq |V(F')|-2
\qquad\text{for every nonempty }F'\subseteq F.                  \tag{5}
\]
By \(\texttt{def:pebble-certificate}\), (5) is equivalent to \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). Such an \(F\) necessarily spans \([T]\), because (5) with \(F'=F\) yields
\[
T-2=|F|\leq |V(F)|-2\leq T-2.                                 \tag{6}
\]

We now relate uniqueness to the linear kernel in (4). If \(\mathcal K(P)=\mathcal L\), any two-dimensional subspace whose restrictions equal the planes in (3) is contained in \(\mathcal K(P)=\mathcal L\), and hence equals \(\mathcal L\). Conversely, suppose the local planes uniquely determine \(\mathcal L\) but \(\mathcal K(P)\supsetneq\mathcal L\). Choose \(h\in\mathcal K(P)\setminus\mathcal L\) and a basis \(u_1,u_2\) of \(\mathcal L\). For \(z\neq0\), set
\[
\mathcal L_z=\operatorname{span}(u_1+zh,u_2).                   \tag{7}
\]
Because \(h\notin\mathcal L\), \(\mathcal L_z\neq\mathcal L\). Equation (4) gives \((\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}\subseteq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\). At \(z=0\), each restriction has rank two by \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\). For each cohort choose a nonzero two-by-two minor of the restricted basis at \(z=0\). Each chosen minor is continuous in \(z\); since \(C<\infty\), all remain nonzero for every sufficiently small \(|z|>0\). Thus \((\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}\) has dimension two and
\[
(\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})
\qquad\text{for every }c\in[C],                                \tag{8}
\]
contradicting uniqueness. Consequently,
\[
r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal K(P)=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma).                       \tag{9}
\]
In particular, if the certificate fails, (9) gives the strict inclusion asserted in the theorem, and the construction (7)--(8) gives the distinct compatible two-dimensional factor plane.

Suppose now that \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). Let \(U\) be any orthonormal basis of the observed-law kernel \(\mathcal K(P)\). By (9) and \(\Gamma^{\prime}\Gamma=I_2\) from \(\texttt{ass:factor-normalization}\), there is an orthogonal matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\) such that \(U=\Gamma W\). The local signal gap implies that \(\Gamma_{S_c}\), and therefore \(U_{S_c}\), has full column rank, so \(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c}\) is positive definite and invertible. With \(G_c=\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}\Gamma_{S_c}\), equation (1) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
U(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c})^{-1}U_{S_c}^{\prime}\nu_c
&=\Gamma W(W^{\prime}G_cW)^{-1}W^{\prime}G_cm_c\\
&=\Gamma WW^{\prime}G_c^{-1}WW^{\prime}G_cm_c\\
&=\Gamma m_c\\
&=\mu_c(P).                                                \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the last equality is the causal response-surface identity following from the factor outcome equation and the conditional mean-zero error restriction; it is not a definition of the causal target. Replacing \(U\) by \(UW_0\) for any orthogonal \(W_0\) leaves the left side of (10) unchanged. Every object on that side is determined by \(P_O\), so (10) is exactly the observed-law map in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-functional}\). If \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\) have \((P_0)_O=(P_1)_O\), their values in (10) coincide for every cohort and time coordinate. This proves entire-observed-law identification when the certificate passes.

It remains to show why the algebraic conclusion under certificate failure cannot be strengthened to causal-target nonidentification under the frozen assumptions. Consider the allowed specification \(T=4\), \(C=1\), and \(S_1=\{1,2,3\}\). Its anchor hypergraph has one edge, hence
\[
r_{1,2}(H_3)=1<T-2=2.                                      \tag{11}
\]
Let
\[
G_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Gamma_0=G_0(G_0^{\prime}G_0)^{-1/2}.                       \tag{12}
\]
Since \(G_0^{\prime}G_0\) is positive definite, \(\Gamma_0^{\prime}\Gamma_0=I_2\). The three two-by-two minors formed from the rows indexed by \(S_1\) are \(1\), \(1\), and \(-1\) before right normalization and remain nonzero afterward. Thus the local restriction has rank two and is generic for this one-edge relation matroid.

Fix \(v>0\), take \(p_1=1\), set \(v_\star=v^\star=v\), and let \(\lambda_i\) be uniform on the circle of radius \(\sqrt{2v}\) in \(\mathbb R^2\). Then
\[
\mathbb E[\lambda_i]=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(\lambda_i)=vI_2,
\qquad
\mathbb E\|\lambda_i\|^{4+\delta}=(2v)^{(4+\delta)/2}.       \tag{13}
\]
Set \(\varepsilon_i=0\) almost surely, choose
\[
M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{(4+\delta)/2},
\qquad
0<g_\star<\lambda_2(\Gamma_{0,S_1}vI_2\Gamma_{0,S_1}^{\prime}), \tag{14}
\]
and choose any \(p_\star\in(0,1)\). Equations (12)--(14) verify rank, normalization, positive loading covariance, local signal gap, conditional homoskedasticity with \(\sigma_1=0\), loading-error orthogonality, and the common moment bound. Independent sampling then gives a nonempty model satisfying every frozen primitive restriction.

For precisely the tight radii in (14), the already-established \(\texttt{lem:tight-moment-radius-forces-zero-means}\) gives
\[
\mu(P)=0\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal M.                \tag{15}
\]
Thus, in this nonempty certificate-failing specification, the causal target is the constant observed-law functional zero even though (9) implies generic factor-plane nonuniqueness. Equations (11)--(15) prove that certificate failure alone does not imply the existence of two observed-law-equivalent laws with different missing means, completing the narrowed theorem.
